entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Iytjenu was an ancient Egyptian king of the First Intermediate Period. Very little is known about him as he is only indirectly attested in the name of a woman called Zat-Iytjenu - Daughter of Iytjenu. The element Iytjenu within the woman's name is written with a royal cartouche. In this period the cartouche was only used for writing a king's name. Therefore, her name must refer to a king. The ruler's name is composed of two elements: Iy and Tjenu, both elements are also well attested as independent names. The position of the king within the First Intermediate Period remains highly speculative.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Iytjenu's existence as a king of the First Intermediate Period has implications for our understanding of ancient Egyptian royal succession and the period's complex political landscape. His indirect attestation through his daughter's name highlights the limited documentation available for this era.
